## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (`python/cudnn/AGENTS.md` Rule 7 -- the DSL gate stays in the stage's `check_support`, before any kernel import; Rule 9 -- one caller contract: the decode form binds the SAME `execute(block_table=, kv_lens=, slot_mapping=)` spelling as the extend form, every unserved spelling is a typed decline the static envelope predicts; `python/cudnn/sdpa/AGENTS.md` Rule S2 -- the tracker rows land in the binding commits, no `Capabilities` / `EngineSpec` change) and my changes comply.
- [x] Labels: `cat-feature`, `area:frost`, `mod-frost`, `orig-nv-eng`.

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL -- the FROST gated attention block (`python/cudnn/gated_attention_block/`), frontend-only Python: a second paged-KV serving form of the block over an existing SDPA kernel (the Rubin d256 decode tile of #1543), the block's static serving-envelope record, the tensor-parallel shard geometries of the Qwen3.5-397B layer pinned in the layout contract and end to end, the attention-inference benchmark's page-size axis, their docs, tests and tracker rows. No C++, no engine row, no new kernel, no change to any SDPA kernel body.

**Builds on merged #1606 and #1617.** This branch incorporates `develop` through the packed-gate merge (`fb3e01e3f`), including #1621’s MXFP8 loop-bound fix. This PR adds paged-KV DECODE, its static serving envelope, tensor-parallel shard contracts, and the inference benchmark’s page-size axis. Packed THD gating and DECODE split-combine gating compose, while paged EXTEND retains its fused-gate decline.

## Summary

The route and API descriptions below reflect this feature’s scope. Numerical measurements and original test counts are retained as historical pre-integration evidence on the stated hardware; they do not claim new integrated-head results.

1. **The DECODE serving form.** A dense `[B, S_q, d_model]` declaration with `kv_source="paged"` over `paged_kv_page_size > 0` -- `GatedAttentionBlockFwd(sample_h, ..., paged_kv_page_size=P, kv_source="paged", sample_k_cache=, sample_v_cache=, sample_block_table=, max_kv_len=None, decode_split_kv=None)` -- writes the step's tokens through into the paged pools and attends, per sequence, over the first `kv_lens[b]` keys of the pages `block_table[b]` lists (the prefix and the step's own tokens) on the bottom-right causal diagonal, on the Rubin d256 decode tile of #1543 (`sdpa/fwd/kernels/sm107/decode_d256_f16.py`: the whole GQA group packed into one tile, the SDPA heuristics' decode split model with fp32 partials in the block's workspace and one combine launch). The per-sequence KV length is ONE fact bound to the KV side only (`seq_kv_lens = kv_lens`, `seq_q_lens = None`: every Q row of the step is live; a serving stack's padded entry -- `kv_lens = 0`, block-table row `0`, slot `-1` -- yields `out` rows exactly `0` and writes nothing to block `0`); `execute(seq_lens=)` is refused under the form. The pools' and the table's strides are declaration samples compiled into the TMA descriptors: HND compact, NHD by strides, the two halves of a unified `[num_pages, H_kv, P, 2D]` content row, and a block table that is a row SLICE of a wider table at any row stride. `fuse_gate=True` rides the decode tile's split COMBINE (the tile has no gate seams; the combine multiplies the merged fp32 value by `sigmoid(G)` before the single cast, the split floored at 2 under the gate); on an unsplit decode tile the gate is its own launch -- `blk.gate_fused` says which runs, `fuse_gate` stays what was declared. The pipeline is `(1)+(2)+(3) -> (4w) -> (4) [+ combine] -> (5) -> (6)`; under a split-KV plan stage (5) is not a launch of its own.

2. **The route is a declaration fact, read off the SDPA adapter's own rule before anything compiles.** `decode_route(geometry, S_q) -> DecodeRoute` names the kernel per `(group = H_q / H_kv, S_q)` exactly as the adapter applies it (`config_sm107.decode_d256_q_tile`), and `_Sdpa.compile` pins the compiled `kernel_template` against it. The table, as `serving_envelope().decode.routes` reports it and the docs print it:

   | `(group, S_q)` | stage (4) | `n_q` / `token_units` / `pack_gqa` |
   |---|---|---|
   | `S_q x group <= 16` | the decode tile, the whole group packed, one token unit (the 16-column tile) | 16 / 1 / True |
   | up to two token units of `32 // group` tokens -- 32 / 2 and 24 / 2: `S_q <= 4`; 8 / 1: `S_q <= 8`; 24 / 4: `S_q <= 10`; 4 / 1: `S_q <= 16` | the 32-column decode tile, `ceil(S_q / (32 // group))` CTAs per (KV head, sequence, split) | 32 / 1 or 2 / True |
   | past the packed route, `S_q <= 32` | the decode tile UNPACKED (the adapter's own rule for a group it does not pack): one Q head per CTA, one token unit | 16 or 32 / 1 / False |
   | `S_q > 32` (`DECODE_MAX_ROWS`) | NOT served: a typed `NotImplementedError` at declaration (the adapter serves dense half queries over paged K / V on the decode tile only; the paged d256 prefill body serves PACKED queries -- the extend form) | tile `None`, `reason` set |

   Per served group and `S_q` 1 / 2 / 3 / 4: group 16 (32 / 2, and the 16 / 1 shard) -- tile 16 packed 1 unit, tile 32 packed 1 unit, tile 32 packed 2 units, tile 32 packed 2 units; group 12 (24 / 2) -- the same four; group 8 (8 / 1) -- tile 16 / 16 / 32 / 32, packed, 1 unit each; group 6 (24 / 4) -- tile 16 / 16 / 32 / 32, packed, 1 unit each; group 4 (4 / 1) -- tile 16, packed, 1 unit at every `S_q <= 4`. `S_q = 5` rides the UNPACKED 16-column tile at groups 16 and 12, the packed 32-column tile's second token unit at 8 / 1, one unit of the 32-column tile at 24 / 4 and at 4 / 1. **The CLAIMED envelope is `1 <= S_q <= DECODE_MAX_S_Q = 4` on the PACKED tile at every served group** (`DecodeRoute.claimed`: one new token plus up to three speculative ones); the wider packed cells of 8 / 1, 24 / 4 and 4 / 1 and the unpacked arm up to 32 rows are routed, declared and correct on the cells run, and **unmeasured** -- no performance claim is made for any arm of the form in this change (the serving perf cells are a separate change). A dense step wider than 32 rows has no kernel over the pools on this part and is the extend form's (packed) business.

3. **`GatedAttentionBlockFwd.serving_envelope(geometry, dtype, device) -> ServingEnvelope`** is the STATIC record a serving stack reads at construction instead of catching exceptions: the forms served (`forms`, drawn from `extend` / `decode`), one record per form (`ExtendEnvelope` / `DecodeEnvelope`: `served`, the `reason` it would decline with, every typed decline of the form in `declines`), `page_sizes` (16 / 32 / 64 / 128), `pool_layouts` (the three stride patterns), the decode route per `(group, S_q)` (`decode.routes` for `S_q` 1 .. 8, `decode.route(s_q)` for any step, `decode.max_s_q` / `decode.max_rows`), the pool dtypes (bf16 / f16; an e4m3 pool is not served) and the part / CuTe DSL facts (`device_cc`, `cutedsl_ok` / `cutedsl_reason`) -- derived from the same helpers the declaration and `check_support` run, so no decline is reachable at `execute` that the record did not predict; a `device_cc=` reading lets a host read another part's envelope. It never raises for a device the block does not serve. The extend half says the sparse declaration's own `thd=True` refusal for a `QsaSpec` geometry (the THD-only form meets it before any row of the table); the dense decode half reaches the table's `sparse` row.

4. **The Qwen3.5-397B tensor-parallel shards pinned end to end** -- 16 / 1 (TP 2), 8 / 1 (TP 4, the serving deployment's shard) and 4 / 1 (TP 8) at `d_model` 4096, `d_head` 256 (the query heads divided across the ranks, the two KV heads divided at TP 2 and replicated from TP 4 on). The layout contract pins `n_qkvg` 8704 / 4608 / 2560 -- every band a whole number of 256-column tiles, so the forced 256-wide GEMM tile of the serving route holds and `qkvg_tile_plan(64 / 128 / 256)` is well defined -- the GQA groups 16 / 8 / 4 and the TMA norm kernel's fitted tile per shard DERIVED from the body (16 / 8 / 4 rows; every shard rides the TMA kernel, the 4-row tile one row per warp). One Rubin end-to-end cell per shard and form within the dense suite's budget (nothing widened), each shard on the kernel block size its deployment allocates; group 4 joins the decode suite's matrix; a shard's route is pinned equal to its group's on the CPU (16 / 1 rides group 16's entries with one KV head).

5. **The attention-inference benchmark gains an appended `page_sizes` axis** (the generation-phase page sizes a paged-KV backend sweeps; the dense cuDNN graph paths run once per case), the runner expands it and runs an unlisted `--backend` alone over the config's axes, and the `qwen35` config sweeps its TP 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 shards at pages 16 / 32 / 64 (192 generation cases for the paged reference backend on a dry run; the default run unchanged at 184 cases).

The `fuse_gate` row of the serving declines table and its `_ServingDecl` field are not in this change, exactly as in #1606: they belong to the THD-gate change (the dense packed prefill's epilogue gate), which carries them. On this branch a packed (`thd=True`) declaration with `fuse_gate=True` keeps the block's own earlier typed decline; the decode form's `fuse_gate` is served as described above.

## Why

A serving stack's decode step is the half of the block the extend form (#1606) does not cover: one new token per sequence (up to four with speculative decoding) over a paged cache, where a prefill-shaped kernel would stream the whole KV range for a handful of query rows. The Rubin d256 decode tile of #1543 is that kernel; this change binds the block to it with the same caller contract as the extend form -- the same pools, the same block table, the same `execute` spelling -- so a stack declares the layer once per form and reads one static envelope instead of probing by exception. The route table is published rather than inferred because an envelope claim is a config claim: a record that names a kernel the plan never runs is the silent-wrong-answer class, so the route is read off the adapter's own rule and the compiled template is pinned against it. The shards are pinned because the deployment runs the layer sharded, and a fitted norm tile no pinned geometry had reached (8 and 4 rows) is exactly what a sentence about the family cannot vouch for.

## Related issues

Builds on merged #1606 (the EXTEND form) and #1543 (the Rubin d256 decode tile). The integrated base also includes #1609’s capture-safe projection route; the historical capture skip reported below describes the earlier PR tree.

## API and compatibility impact

- New public names (`docs/fe-oss-apis/api_conventions.md` read against each: records, constants and a function named by op geometry -- no op function, no architecture or implementation technology in a name; the API index gains exactly these eleven rows): `DecodeEnvelope` (`inference_only`, `writes_lse`, `route(s_q)`), `DecodeRoute` (`served`, `decode_tile`, `reason`), `decode_route(geometry, s_q)`, `DECODE_MAX_S_Q = 4`, `DECODE_MAX_ROWS = 32`. #1606's `ServingEnvelope` gains its `decode` record beside `extend` (the `serving_envelope` classmethod, `ExtendEnvelope`, `SERVING_PAGE_SIZES` / `SERVING_POOL_LAYOUTS` and `KV_SOURCE_SELF` / `KV_SOURCE_PAGED` are #1606's names and keep their meaning; `serving_envelope` gains an APPENDED `device_cc=` keyword for a host-side reading of another part's envelope). `GatedAttentionBlockFwd` gains `max_kv_len` and `decode_split_kv` APPENDED after the existing keyword arguments (defaults `None`), and `decode_route` / `decode_split_kv` / `gate_fused` as declaration facts. `import cudnn` still pulls neither torch nor the DSL (pinned).
- `execute(seq_lens=)` under `kv_source="paged"` is a typed refusal (the dense block's self-attention length is a Q-side length; the KV length is `kv_lens`). Every other declaration keeps its behaviour: `kv_source="self"` is unchanged and refuses every paged-read input rather than ignoring it.
- The benchmark config type gains `page_sizes` at the END (append-only; default = the former behaviour).
- `Capabilities` / `EngineSpec` / manifest: unchanged (the block has no engine row). Tracker rows (Rule S2): the DECODE form's rows (form x layout x page x dtype, the route per group, the shards) in the binding commits.
- GPU / versions: the decode form needs Rubin cc 10.7 (the decode tile's part) and the same DSL floor as the block; off Rubin the envelope reads `served = False` and the declaration is a typed decline naming the part. No numerics change on any existing path.

## Testing

### Final review fixes and integration — 2026-10-14

At `3d714a9835f062bc1ccfef43f130a31f07a90223`, all **33 focused Rubin integration checks passed, 0 skipped**: DECODE declarations and envelope, split-combine gating, first-execute capture, EXTEND declines, packed gated cache write-through, and packed THD gate numerics. The run used the matching gate-capable native extension and verified the worktree imports.

The benchmark now records and deduplicates the effective b12x page size while preserving absorbed-MLA and contiguous routes. All **6 CPU benchmark regression tests passed** (the unfixed runner failed 5). The CPU declaration fix changed **25 failures to 25 passes**, with the split-heuristic control and three gate-admission checks also passing. Stale DECODE documentation was corrected. Formatting and independent integration review passed.

Earlier native and CI results below retain their original source attribution. The queued Rubin CI jobs have not executed tests; these local Rubin runs provide the native correctness evidence for this integration.


### Integrated-head validation — 2026-10-13

At `b519411c468cd8496515147018006f96feadbd10`, the Rubin correctness rerun passed **436 tests, 0 skipped**, covering all levels of the DECODE, EXTEND, end-to-end, layout-contract and core import-boundary suites. This includes the integrated capture, pool-layout and hypothetical-target regressions.

Environment: SM107, cuDNN 9.27, CuTeDSL 4.8.0, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Python 3.10.22. The runner verified the exact clean source head, source hashes, worktree imports and the recorded native extension hash. Pytest returned 0 and the JUnit report had no failures, errors or skips. These are shared-hardware functional checks; no performance measurement is claimed.

### Historical validation

The measurements and validation counts below are the original pre-integration evidence, retained with their stated hardware and scope. They do not claim a new run on the integrated head.

Rubin (cc 10.7, a 204-SM development node; functional cells, never a perf number), run on the development tree these commits come from:

- `test_block_serving_decode.py` (L0): **96 passed** -- every served group (32 / 2, 24 / 2, 8 / 1, 24 / 4, 4 / 1) x `S_q` 1 .. 5 against the per-sequence fp32 oracle (cos 0.999987 .. 0.999996 on `out`; bf16 max |diff| <= 1.465e-3, f16 1.221e-4; `kv_lens` 100 / 384 / 500 / 0: a tail tile, the ring depth exactly, four tiles, a padded entry whose `out` rows are exactly 0 with block 0's bytes untouched); the three pool layouts BITWISE at pages 16 / 32 / 64 / 128, bf16 and f16; the block bitwise the standalone SDPA adapter on the same views; paged == dense bitwise (O and LSE) at the unsplit plan; split 4 == unsplit within the combine's derived two-term budget on the pre-gate O (0.26 / 0.16 of it at 32 / 2 and 8 / 1; the fp32 LSEs to 1e-6); the gate in the combine vs the separate gate launch within the one-rounding budget (max |diff| 9.766e-4 bf16 / 1.221e-4 f16 on O, 0.73 / 0.83 of it); a row-sliced block table at row stride 37 bitwise the compact one; `kv_lens` 128 / 384 / 512 / 1024 and `kv_lens == S_q`; the first execute of a fresh declaration captured on a new stream with no warm-up under `set_sync_debug_mode("error")`, the replay bitwise eager, new lengths / tables / slots / inputs through the captured tensors bitwise the eager run; `get_workspace_size()` honest (the split partials inside, a sentinel past it untouched); two launches bitwise; the compiled kernel pinned against the declared route (template, packing, split, `epilogue_gate` False). 12 fresh processes at `kv_lens = 128 x n_kv`, `n_kv` in {1, 2, 4, 8}: ok 12 / hang 0 / other 0.
- `test_block_serving_extend.py`: **171 passed** (the row-by-row envelope pin with the decode rows and the `device_cc` reading; the 16 / 1, 8 / 1 and 4 / 1 shard cells: two sequences at `T_max` 256, a 100-token step over a 60-row prefix and a 156-token step over a 100-row prefix, worst `out` cos 0.999994 / 0.999994 / 0.999995, gated-O max abs err 7.812e-3 / 3.906e-3 / 3.906e-3 of the 2e-2 budget); `test_block_end_to_end.py`: **60 passed** (the dense shard cells, B = 1, S = 512, HF-form weights: `out` cos 0.999995 / 0.999996 / 0.999995 vs the oracle on the block's weights, the norm stage pinned on the TMA kernel at the fitted tile); `test_layout_contract.py`: **76 passed** (CPU). The decode shard cells: `S_q = 1` over `kv_lens` 100 / 384 / 500 / 0 at pages 16 / 32 / 64, `out` cos 0.999988 / 0.999988 / 0.999987.

On the historical pre-integration PR tree, a Rubin node of the 212-SM class (cc 10.7; functional cells, one process per module, `cudnn` imported from the PR tree): `test_block_serving_decode.py` -> **96 passed** (141 s: every group x `S_q` cell, the pool matrix, the padded entries, the row-sliced table, the split / unsplit and gate-in-combine cells, the capture replay, the workspace and route pins); `test_block_serving_extend.py` -> **170 passed, 1 skipped** (85 s; the skip in that historical run was the capture cell, before integration of #1609's capture-safe projection route); `test_block_end_to_end.py` -> **60 passed** (60 s); `test_layout_contract.py` -> **76 passed** (3 s); the shard cells re-run with their magnitudes printed -> **9 passed**: DECODE `out` cos vs the oracle 0.999990 / 0.999988 / 0.999989 at 16 / 1 (page 16), 8 / 1 (page 32), 4 / 1 (page 64), max |diff| 3.906e-3 / 1.953e-3 / 9.766e-4; EXTEND worst `out` cos 0.999995 / 0.999994 / 0.999994 with gated-O max |err| 3.906e-3 at every shard (budget 2e-2); the dense shard cells within the suite's budget. Both GPUs of the node were idle before and after the run, the SM clock at its lock; no number here is a performance claim.

**🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**`test_declaration_facts` fails on a host without CUDA, but the module says it supports one.**

The module docstring says the declaration cells run "even on the CPU", and `_DEV` falls back to `"cpu"`. On such a host, `_check_serving_declaration` passes `sm_count=0` to `decode_split_choice`. That function returns 1 before it applies the gated floor of 2. As a result, `decode_split_kv == 1` and `gate_fused` is False even with `fuse_gate=True`. The assertion `blk.decode_split_kv >= 2 and blk.gate_fused and blk._gate is None` on Line 451 then fails, and so does the stage-list assertion on Line 453.

Pin the split for the fused-gate facts. The heuristic choice is already covered by `test_the_split_choice_is_the_decode_split_model_floored_at_two_under_the_gate`.

<summary>💚 Proposed fix</summary>

+++ "b/test/python/gated_attention_block/cutedsl/test_block_serving_decode.py"
@@ -444,7 +444,8 @@
 def test_declaration_facts(group, s_q):
     """A declared DECODE block records its route, its split and where the gate runs BEFORE anything compiles; the stage list
     is the serving pipeline; both projections are capture-safe; ``seq_lens_present`` reads True whatever was passed."""
-    blk, _ = _make_block(group, 4, s_q, fuse_gate=True, fuse_norm_rope=True)
+    # pin the split: off CUDA (sm_count 0) the decode split model returns 1 and the gate would not ride the combine
+    blk, _ = _make_block(group, 4, s_q, fuse_gate=True, fuse_norm_rope=True, decode_split_kv=None if torch.cuda.is_available() else 2)
     r = blk.decode_route
     assert r == decode_route(blk.geom, s_q) and blk.kv_source == "paged" and blk.max_kv_len == 64 * 16 and blk.seq_lens_present is True
     assert blk._sdpa.paged_dense and blk._sdpa.decode_route == r and blk._sdpa.decode_split_kv == blk.decode_split_kv and blk._sdpa.seq_lens_present

+_SENTINEL = 1024.0  # the pools' fill: FINITE (a serving stack's cache is zero-initialized; the tail tile reads and masks the rows past kv_len)
+
+
+def _cc():
+    return tuple(torch.cuda.get_device_capability()) if torch.cuda.is_available() else None
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def _no_host_sync():
+    """Every declaration-time and form check stays on the host without a device sync (Rule 3) -- enforced, not read."""
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        yield
+        return
+    prev = torch.cuda.get_sync_debug_mode()
+    torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode(prev)
+
+
+def _geom(group, heads=None, **over):
+    """The block geometry (and the oracle's mirror) of ``group``: the shrunk matrix's heads, or an explicit ``(h_q, h_kv)`` of that
+    group (the 397B shards at their real ``d_model``, passed through ``over``)."""
+    h_q, h_kv = _GROUPS[group] if heads is None else heads
+    assert h_q % h_kv == 0 and h_q // h_kv == group, (group, heads)
+    kw = dict(d_model=_D_MODEL, h_q=h_q, h_kv=h_kv, d_head=_D, rope_dim=_ROPE, causal_bottom_right=True)
+    kw.update(over)
+    return GatedAttentionBlockGeometry(**kw), RefGeometry(**kw)
+
+
+def _cos(a, b):
+    a, b = a.float().flatten(), b.float().flatten()
+    return (a @ b / (a.norm() * b.norm())).item()
+
+
+def _bits(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """The 16-bit patterns of a bf16 / f16 tensor: a NaN-safe bitwise comparison (the sentinel is NaN)."""
+    return x.contiguous().view(torch.int16)
+
+
+def _pools(n_pages, h, page_size, d, layout, dtype, device=_DEV, fill=None):
+    """Two sentinel-filled pools as ``[P, H, page_size, D]`` views -- ``hnd`` (L1, compact), ``nhd`` (L2, by strides), ``unified``
+    (L3: ONE ``[P, H, page_size, 2D]`` content row per token, K at ``+0``, V at ``+D``).  The fill is a large FINITE value
+    (``_SENTINEL``): the decode tile's tail tile reads the rows past ``kv_len`` (the last page's stale rows, block 0 for the
+    pages a short row does not list) and masks them to ``P = 0`` -- exactly 0 for a finite value, NaN for a NaN one (``0 x
+    NaN``); a serving stack's cache is zero-initialized, so finite is the contract and a big sentinel is the detector of an
+    unmasked read."""
+    fill = _SENTINEL if fill is None else fill
+    if layout == "hnd":
+        return tuple(torch.full((n_pages, h, page_size, d), fill, device=device, dtype=dtype) for _ in range(2))
+    if layout == "nhd":
+        return tuple(torch.full((n_pages, page_size, h, d), fill, device=device, dtype=dtype).permute(0, 2, 1, 3) for _ in range(2))
+    assert layout == "unified"
+    row = torch.full((n_pages, h, page_size, 2 * d), fill, device=device, dtype=dtype)
+    return row[..., :d], row[..., d:]
+
+
+def _make_block(group, batch, s_q, *, page=16, layout="hnd", n_pages=64, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=_DEV, table_row_stride=None, **blk_kw):
+    """A declared (not compiled) DECODE block on EMPTY tensors: the declaration cells."""
+    geom, _ = _geom(group)
+    h_q, h_kv = _GROUPS[group]
+    mk = lambda *shape: torch.empty(*shape, dtype=dtype, device=device)  # noqa: E731
+    kc, vc = _pools(n_pages, h_kv, page, _D, layout, dtype, device)
+    if table_row_stride is None:
+        bt = torch.zeros(batch, n_pages, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    else:
+        bt = torch.zeros(batch, table_row_stride, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)[:, :n_pages]
+    kw = dict(paged_kv_page_size=page, kv_source="paged", sample_k_cache=kc, sample_v_cache=vc, sample_block_table=bt)
+    kw.update(blk_kw)
+    blk = GatedAttentionBlockFwd(
+        mk(batch, s_q, _D_MODEL),
+        mk(geom.n_qkvg, _D_MODEL),
+        torch.ones(_D, dtype=dtype, device=device),
+        torch.ones(_D, dtype=dtype, device=device),
+        mk(batch, s_q, _ROPE),
+        mk(batch, s_q, _ROPE),
+        mk(_D_MODEL, h_q * _D),
+        mk(batch, s_q, _D_MODEL),
+        geom,
+        **kw,
+    )
+    return blk, dict(k_cache=kc, v_cache=vc, block_table=bt, geom=geom)

+def test_the_route_table_per_group_and_s_q_is_the_adapters_rule(group):
+    """The decode route at every served group against the adapter's rule: the 16-column tile for <= 16 packed rows, the
+    32-column tile in ``ceil(S_q / (32 // G))`` token units up to two, then the UNPACKED arm (one head per CTA) up to 32
+    rows, NOT SERVED past that (the reason names the EXTEND form); the CLAIMED envelope is ``S_q <= 4`` everywhere, the
+    wider cells routed but not claimed.  MHA stays unpacked."""
+    geom, _ = _geom(group)
+    for s_q, (n_q, units, packed) in _ROUTE_TABLE[group].items():
+        r = decode_route(geom, s_q)
+        assert isinstance(r, DecodeRoute) and r.s_q == s_q and r.group == group
+        assert (r.n_q, r.token_units, r.pack_gqa) == (n_q, units, packed), (group, s_q, r)
+        assert r.tile == (DECODE_TILE if n_q else None) and r.decode_tile is bool(n_q) and r.served is bool(n_q)
+        assert (r.reason == "") is bool(n_q) and ("EXTEND form" in r.reason or n_q)
+        assert r.claimed is (packed and s_q <= DECODE_MAX_S_Q)
+        if packed:
+            assert units == -(-s_q // (n_q // group))
+        elif n_q:
+            assert units == 1 and s_q <= n_q
+    mha = GatedAttentionBlockGeometry(d_model=_D_MODEL, h_q=4, h_kv=4, d_head=_D, rope_dim=_ROPE, causal_bottom_right=True)
+    r = decode_route(mha, 2)

detail.body:
## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (`python/cudnn/AGENTS.md` Rule 7 -- the DSL gate stays in the stage's `check_support`, before any kernel import; Rule 9 -- one caller contract: the decode form binds the SAME `execute(block_table=, kv_lens=, slot_mapping=)` spelling as the extend form, every unserved spelling is a typed decline the static envelope predicts; `python/cudnn/sdpa/AGENTS.md` Rule S2 -- the tracker rows land in the binding commits, no `Capabilities` / `EngineSpec` change) and my changes comply.
- [x] Labels: `cat-feature`, `area:frost`, `mod-frost`, `orig-nv-eng`.

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL -- the FROST gated attention block (`python/cudnn/gated_attention_block/`), frontend-only Python: a second paged-KV serving form of the block over an existing SDPA kernel (the Rubin d256 decode tile of #1543), the block's static serving-envelope record, the tensor-parallel shard geometries of the Qwen3.5-397B layer pinned in the layout contract and end to end, the attention-inference benchmark's page-size axis, their docs, tests and tracker rows. No C++, no engine row, no new kernel, no change to any SDPA kernel body.

**Builds on merged #1606 and #1617.** This branch incorporates `develop` through the packed-gate merge (`fb3e01e3f`), including #1621’s MXFP8 loop-bound fix. This PR adds paged-KV DECODE, its static serving envelope, tensor-parallel shard contracts, and the inference benchmark’s page-size axis. Packed THD gating and DECODE split-combine gating compose, while paged EXTEND retains its fused-gate decline.

## Summary

The route and API descriptions below reflect this feature’s scope. Numerical measurements and original test counts are retained as historical pre-integration evidence on the stated hardware; they do not claim new integrated-head results.

1. **The DECODE serving form.** A dense `[B, S_q, d_model]` declaration with `kv_source="paged"` over `paged_kv_page_size > 0` -- `GatedAttentionBlockFwd(sample_h, ..., paged_kv_page_size=P, kv_source="paged", sample_k_cache=, sample_v_cache=, sample_block_table=, max_kv_len=None, decode_split_kv=None)` -- writes the step's tokens through into the paged pools and attends, per sequence, over the first `kv_lens[b]` keys of the pages `block_table[b]` lists (the prefix and the step's own tokens) on the bottom-right causal diagonal, on the Rubin d256 decode tile of #1543 (`sdpa/fwd/kernels/sm107/decode_d256_f16.py`: the whole GQA group packed into one tile, the SDPA heuristics' decode split model with fp32 partials in the block's workspace and one combine launch). The per-sequence KV length is ONE fact bound to the KV side only (`seq_kv_lens = kv_lens`, `seq_q_lens = None`: every Q row of the step is live; a serving stack's padded entry -- `kv_lens = 0`, block-table row `0`, slot `-1` -- yields `out` rows exactly `0` and writes nothing to block `0`); `execute(seq_lens=)` is refused under the form. The pools' and the table's strides are declaration samples compiled into the TMA descriptors: HND compact, NHD by strides, the two halves of a unified `[num_pages, H_kv, P, 2D]` content row, and a block table that is a row SLICE of a wider table at any row stride. `fuse_gate=True` rides the decode tile's split COMBINE (the tile has no gate seams; the combine multiplies the merged fp32 value by `sigmoid(G)` before the single cast, the split floored at 2 under the gate); on an unsplit decode tile the gate is its own launch -- `blk.gate_fused` says which runs, `fuse_gate` stays what was declared. The pipeline is `(1)+(2)+(3) -> (4w) -> (4) [+ combine] -> (5) -> (6)`; under a split-KV plan stage (5) is not a launch of its own.

2. **The route is a declaration fact, read off the SDPA adapter's own rule before anything compiles.** `decode_route(geometry, S_q) -> DecodeRoute` names the kernel per `(group = H_q / H_kv, S_q)` exactly as the adapter applies it (`config_sm107.decode_d256_q_tile`), and `_Sdpa.compile` pins the compiled `kernel_template` against it. The table, as `serving_envelope().decode.routes` reports it and the docs print it:

   | `(group, S_q)` | stage (4) | `n_q` / `token_units` / `pack_gqa` |
   |---|---|---|
   | `S_q x group <= 16` | the decode tile, the whole group packed, one token unit (the 16-column tile) | 16 / 1 / True |
   | up to two token units of `32 // group` tokens -- 32 / 2 and 24 / 2: `S_q <= 4`; 8 / 1: `S_q <= 8`; 24 / 4: `S_q <= 10`; 4 / 1: `S_q <= 16` | the 32-column decode tile, `ceil(S_q / (32 // group))` CTAs per (KV head, sequence, split) | 32 / 1 or 2 / True |
   | past the packed route, `S_q <= 32` | the decode tile UNPACKED (the adapter's own rule for a group it does not pack): one Q head per CTA, one token unit | 16 or 32 / 1 / False |
   | `S_q > 32` (`DECODE_MAX_ROWS`) | NOT served: a typed `NotImplementedError` at declaration (the adapter serves dense half queries over paged K / V on the decode tile only; the paged d256 prefill body serves PACKED queries -- the extend form) | tile `None`, `reason` set |

   Per served group and `S_q` 1 / 2 / 3 / 4: group 16 (32 / 2, and the 16 / 1 shard) -- tile 16 packed 1 unit, tile 32 packed 1 unit, tile 32 packed 2 units, tile 32 packed 2 units; group 12 (24 / 2) -- the same four; group 8 (8 / 1) -- tile 16 / 16 / 32 / 32, packed, 1 unit each; group 6 (24 / 4) -- tile 16 / 16 / 32 / 32, packed, 1 unit each; group 4 (4 / 1) -- tile 16, packed, 1 unit at every `S_q <= 4`. `S_q = 5` rides the UNPACKED 16-column tile at groups 16 and 12, the packed 32-column tile's second token unit at 8 / 1, one unit of the 32-column tile at 24 / 4 and at 4 / 1. **The CLAIMED envelope is `1 <= S_q <= DECODE_MAX_S_Q = 4` on the PACKED tile at every served group** (`DecodeRoute.claimed`: one new token plus up to three speculative ones); the wider packed cells of 8 / 1, 24 / 4 and 4 / 1 and the unpacked arm up to 32 rows are routed, declared and correct on the cells run, and **unmeasured** -- no performance claim is made for any arm of the form in this change (the serving perf cells are a separate change). A dense step wider than 32 rows has no kernel over the pools on this part and is the extend form's (packed) business.

3. **`GatedAttentionBlockFwd.serving_envelope(geometry, dtype, device) -> ServingEnvelope`** is the STATIC record a serving stack reads at construction instead of catching exceptions: the forms served (`forms`, drawn from `extend` / `decode`), one record per form (`ExtendEnvelope` / `DecodeEnvelope`: `served`, the `reason` it would decline with, every typed decline of the form in `declines`), `page_sizes` (16 / 32 / 64 / 128), `pool_layouts` (the three stride patterns), the decode route per `(group, S_q)` (`decode.routes` for `S_q` 1 .. 8, `decode.route(s_q)` for any step, `decode.max_s_q` / `decode.max_rows`), the pool dtypes (bf16 / f16; an e4m3 pool is not served) and the part / CuTe DSL facts (`device_cc`, `cutedsl_ok` / `cutedsl_reason`) -- derived from the same helpers the declaration and `check_support` run, so no decline is reachable at `execute` that the record did not predict; a `device_cc=` reading lets a host read another part's envelope. It never raises for a device the block does not serve. The extend half says the sparse declaration's own `thd=True` refusal for a `QsaSpec` geometry (the THD-only form meets it before any row of the table); the dense decode half reaches the table's `sparse` row.

4. **The Qwen3.5-397B tensor-parallel shards pinned end to end** -- 16 / 1 (TP 2), 8 / 1 (TP 4, the serving deployment's shard) and 4 / 1 (TP 8) at `d_model` 4096, `d_head` 256 (the query heads divided across the ranks, the two KV heads divided at TP 2 and replicated from TP 4 on). The layout contract pins `n_qkvg` 8704 / 4608 / 2560 -- every band a whole number of 256-column tiles, so the forced 256-wide GEMM tile of the serving route holds and `qkvg_tile_plan(64 / 128 / 256)` is well defined -- the GQA groups 16 / 8 / 4 and the TMA norm kernel's fitted tile per shard DERIVED from the body (16 / 8 / 4 rows; every shard rides the TMA kernel, the 4-row tile one row per warp). One Rubin end-to-end cell per shard and form within the dense suite's budget (nothing widened), each shard on the kernel block size its deployment allocates; group 4 joins the decode suite's matrix; a shard's route is pinned equal to its group's on the CPU (16 / 1 rides group 16's entries with one KV head).

5. **The attention-inference benchmark gains an appended `page_sizes` axis** (the generation-phase page sizes a paged-KV backend sweeps; the dense cuDNN graph paths run once per case), the runner expands it and runs an unlisted `--backend` alone over the config's axes, and the `qwen35` config sweeps its TP 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 shards at pages 16 / 32 / 64 (192 generation cases for the paged reference backend on a dry run; the default run unchanged at 184 cases).

The `fuse_gate` row of the serving declines table and its `_ServingDecl` field are not in this change, exactly as in #1606: they belong to the THD-gate change (the dense packed prefill's epilogue gate), which carries them. On this branch a packed (`thd=True`) declaration with `fuse_gate=True` keeps the block's own earlier typed decline; the decode form's `fuse_gate` is served as described above.

## Why

A serving stack's decode step is the half of the block the extend form (#1606) does not cover: one new token per sequence (up to four with speculative decoding) over a paged cache, where a prefill-shaped kernel would stream the whole KV range for a handful of query rows. The Rubin d256 decode tile of #1543 is that kernel; this change binds the block to it with the same caller contract as the extend form -- the same pools, the same block table, the same `execute` spelling -- so a stack declares the layer once per form and reads one static envelope instead of probing by exception. The route table is published rather than inferred because an envelope claim is a config claim: a record that names a kernel the plan never runs is the silent-wrong-answer class, so the route is read off the adapter's own rule and the compiled template is pinned against it. The shards are pinned because the deployment runs the layer sharded, and a fitted norm tile no pinned geometry had reached (8 and 4 rows) is exactly what a sentence about the family cannot vouch for.

## Related issues

Builds on merged #1606 (the EXTEND form) and #1543 (the Rubin d256 decode tile). The integrated base also includes #1609’s capture-safe projection route; the historical capture skip reported below describes the earlier PR tree.

## API and compatibility impact

- New public names (`docs/fe-oss-apis/api_conventions.md` read against each: records, constants and a function named by op geometry -- no op function, no architecture or implementation technology in a name; the API index gains exactly these eleven rows): `DecodeEnvelope` (`inference_only`, `writes_lse`, `route(s_q)`), `DecodeRoute` (`served`, `decode_tile`, `reason`), `decode_route(geometry, s_q)`, `DECODE_MAX_S_Q = 4`, `DECODE_MAX_ROWS = 32`. #1606's `ServingEnvelope` gains its `decode` record beside `extend` (the `serving_envelope` classmethod, `ExtendEnvelope`, `SERVING_PAGE_SIZES` / `SERVING_POOL_LAYOUTS` and `KV_SOURCE_SELF` / `KV_SOURCE_PAGED` are #1606's names and keep their meaning; `serving_envelope` gains an APPENDED `device_cc=` keyword for a host-side reading of another part's envelope). `GatedAttentionBlockFwd` gains `max_kv_len` and `decode_split_kv` APPENDED after the existing keyword arguments (defaults `None`), and `decode_route` / `decode_split_kv` / `gate_fused` as declaration facts. `import cudnn` still pulls neither torch nor the DSL (pinned).
- `execute(seq_lens=)` under `kv_source="paged"` is a typed refusal (the dense block's self-attention length is a Q-side length; the KV length is `kv_lens`). Every other declaration keeps its behaviour: `kv_source="self"` is unchanged and refuses every paged-read input rather than ignoring it.
- The benchmark config type gains `page_sizes` at the END (append-only; default = the former behaviour).
- `Capabilities` / `EngineSpec` / manifest: unchanged (the block has no engine row). Tracker rows (Rule S2): the DECODE form's rows (form x layout x page x dtype, the route per group, the shards) in the binding commits.
- GPU / versions: the decode form needs Rubin cc 10.7 (the decode tile's part) and the same DSL floor as the block; off Rubin the envelope reads `served = False` and the declaration is a typed decline naming the part. No numerics change on any existing path.

## Testing

### Final review fixes and integration — 2026-10-14

At `3d714a9835f062bc1ccfef43f130a31f07a90223`, all **33 focused Rubin integration checks passed, 0 skipped**: DECODE declarations and envelope, split-combine gating, first-execute capture, EXTEND declines, packed gated cache write-through, and packed THD gate numerics. The run used the matching gate-capable native extension and verified the worktree imports.

The benchmark now records and deduplicates the effective b12x page size while preserving absorbed-MLA and contiguous routes. All **6 CPU benchmark regression tests passed** (the unfixed runner failed 5). The CPU declaration fix changed **25 failures to 25 passes**, with the split-heuristic control and three gate-admission checks also passing. Stale DECODE documentation was corrected. Formatting and independent integration review passed.

Earlier native and CI results below retain their original source attribution. The queued Rubin CI jobs have not executed tests; these local Rubin runs provide the native correctness evidence for this integration.


### Integrated-head validation — 2026-10-13

At `b519411c468cd8496515147018006f96feadbd10`, the Rubin correctness rerun passed **436 tests, 0 skipped**, covering all levels of the DECODE, EXTEND, end-to-end, layout-contract and core import-boundary suites. This includes the integrated capture, pool-layout and hypothetical-target regressions.

Environment: SM107, cuDNN 9.27, CuTeDSL 4.8.0, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Python 3.10.22. The runner verified the exact clean source head, source hashes, worktree imports and the recorded native extension hash. Pytest returned 0 and the JUnit report had no failures, errors or skips. These are shared-hardware functional checks; no performance measurement is claimed.

### Historical validation

The measurements and validation counts below are the original pre-integration evidence, retained with their stated hardware and scope. They do not claim a new run on the integrated head.

Rubin (cc 10.7, a 204-SM development node; functional cells, never a perf number), run on the development tree these commits come from:

- `test_block_serving_decode.py` (L0): **96 passed** -- every served group (32 / 2, 24 / 2, 8 / 1, 24 / 4, 4 / 1) x `S_q` 1 .. 5 against the per-sequence fp32 oracle (cos 0.999987 .. 0.999996 on `out`; bf16 max |diff| <= 1.465e-3, f16 1.221e-4; `kv_lens` 100 / 384 / 500 / 0: a tail tile, the ring depth exactly, four tiles, a padded entry whose `out` rows are exactly 0 with block 0's bytes untouched); the three pool layouts BITWISE at pages 16 / 32 / 64 / 128, bf16 and f16; the block bitwise the standalone SDPA adapter on the same views; paged == dense bitwise (O and LSE) at the unsplit plan; split 4 == unsplit within the combine's derived two-term budget on the pre-gate O (0.26 / 0.16 of it at 32 / 2 and 8 / 1; the fp32 LSEs to 1e-6); the gate in the combine vs the separate gate launch within the one-rounding budget (max |diff| 9.766e-4 bf16 / 1.221e-4 f16 on O, 0.73 / 0.83 of it); a row-sliced block table at row stride 37 bitwise the compact one; `kv_lens` 128 / 384 / 512 / 1024 and `kv_lens == S_q`; the first execute of a fresh declaration captured on a new stream with no warm-up under `set_sync_debug_mode("error")`, the replay bitwise eager, new lengths / tables / slots / inputs through the captured tensors bitwise the eager run; `get_workspace_size()` honest (the split partials inside, a sentinel past it untouched); two launches bitwise; the compiled kernel pinned against the declared route (template, packing, split, `epilogue_gate` False). 12 fresh processes at `kv_lens = 128 x n_kv`, `n_kv` in {1, 2, 4, 8}: ok 12 / hang 0 / other 0.
- `test_block_serving_extend.py`: **171 passed** (the row-by-row envelope pin with the decode rows and the `device_cc` reading; the 16 / 1, 8 / 1 and 4 / 1 shard cells: two sequences at `T_max` 256, a 100-token step over a 60-row prefix and a 156-token step over a 100-row prefix, worst `out` cos 0.999994 / 0.999994 / 0.999995, gated-O max abs err 7.812e-3 / 3.906e-3 / 3.906e-3 of the 2e-2 budget); `test_block_end_to_end.py`: **60 passed** (the dense shard cells, B = 1, S = 512, HF-form weights: `out` cos 0.999995 / 0.999996 / 0.999995 vs the oracle on the block's weights, the norm stage pinned on the TMA kernel at the fitted tile); `test_layout_contract.py`: **76 passed** (CPU). The decode shard cells: `S_q = 1` over `kv_lens` 100 / 384 / 500 / 0 at pages 16 / 32 / 64, `out` cos 0.999988 / 0.999988 / 0.999987.

On the historical pre-integration PR tree, a Rubin node of the 212-SM class (cc 10.7; functional cells, one process per module, `cudnn` imported from the PR tree): `test_block_serving_decode.py` -> **96 passed** (141 s: every group x `S_q` cell, the pool matrix, the padded entries, the row-sliced table, the split / unsplit and gate-in-combine cells, the capture replay, the workspace and route pins); `test_block_serving_extend.py` -> **170 passed, 1 skipped** (85 s; the skip in that historical run was the capture cell, before integration of #1609's capture-safe projection route); `test_block_end_to_end.py` -> **60 passed** (60 s); `test_layout_contract.py` -> **76 passed** (3 s); the shard cells re-run with their magnitudes printed -> **9 passed**: DECODE `out` cos vs the oracle 0.999990 / 0.999988 / 0.999989 at 16 / 1 (page 16), 8 / 1 (page 32), 4 / 1 (page 64), max |diff| 3.906e-3 / 1.953e-3 / 9.766e-4; EXTEND worst `out` cos 0.999995 / 0.999994 / 0.999994 with gated-O max |err| 3.906e-3 at every shard (budget 2e-2); the dense shard cells within the suite's budget. +

+from benchmark.attention_inference.config_types import InferenceBenchmarkConfig, ModelPreset
+from benchmark.attention_inference.configs.qwen35 import CONFIG as QWEN35
+from benchmark.attention_inference.runner import InferenceBenchmarkRunner
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.L0
+
+
+class PageSizeTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.runner = InferenceBenchmarkRunner()
+        self.model = ModelPreset("gqa", num_q_heads=8, num_kv_heads=2)
+        self.config = InferenceBenchmarkConfig(
+            "pages",
+            models=[self.model],
+            generation_shapes=[(1, 256)],
+            generation_batch_sizes=[1],
+            backends=["b12x"],
+            page_size=16,
+            page_sizes=[16, 32, 64],
+        )
+
+    def pages(self, **changes):
+        return [case["page_size"] for case in self.runner.expand_config(replace(self.config, **changes))]
+
+    def test_b12x_paged_cases_use_unique_effective_sizes_in_order(self):
+        self.assertEqual(self.pages(), [64])
+        self.assertEqual(self.pages(page_sizes=[128, 32, 64, 16, 128]), [128, 64])
+        self.assertEqual(self.pages(page_sizes=None), [64])
+        self.assertEqual(self.pages(page_sizes=[]), [64])
+
+    def test_b12x_absorbed_mla_routes_keep_their_distinct_page_contracts(self):
+        mla = replace(self.model, kind="mla_absorbed", head_dim_qk=576, head_dim_vo=512)
+        self.assertEqual(self.pages(models=[mla]), [16, 32, 64])
+        self.assertEqual(self.pages(models=[mla], page_sizes=None), [16])
+        shared_kv = replace(mla, head_dim_qk=512)
+        self.assertEqual(self.pages(models=[shared_kv]), [64])
+
+    def test_b12x_dense_fallback_and_context_do_not_sweep_pages(self):
+        sliding = replace(self.model, sliding_window_size=128)
+        self.assertEqual(self.pages(models=[sliding]), [16])
+        self.assertEqual(self.pages(context_seqlens=[128], generation_shapes=[]), [16])
+
+    def test_other_backends_keep_their_page_axes(self):
+        for backend in ("flashinfer", "flash_mla"):
+            with self.subTest(backend=backend):
+                self.assertEqual(self.pages(backends=[backend], page_sizes=[32, 16, 32, 64]), [32, 16, 64])
+        for backend in ("cudnn", "cudnn_oss", "flash_attention_4"):
+            with self.subTest(backend=backend):
+                self.assertEqual(self.pages(backends=[backend]), [16])
+
+    def test_effective_size_reaches_subprocess_and_result_metadata(self):
+        cases = list(self.runner.expand_config(self.config))
+        self.assertEqual(len(cases), 1)
+        with patch(
+            "benchmark.attention_inference.runner.subprocess.run",
+            return_value=subprocess.CompletedProcess([], 0, stdout="RESULT,1,2,3,,test-device,b12x paged (page=64)\n"),
+        ) as run:
+            result = self.runner.run_single(cases[0], cc=(12, 0))
+        cmd = run.call_args.args[0]
+        self.assertEqual(cmd[cmd.index("--page_size") + 1], "64")
+        self.assertTrue(result.success)
+        self.assertEqual(result.page_size, 64)
+
+    def test_qwen35_counts_distinct_executed_page_sizes(self):
+        self.assertEqual(len(list(self.runner.expand_config(QWEN35))), 184)
+        for backend, count, pages in (("flashinfer", 192, {16, 32, 64}), ("b12x", 64, {64})):
+            with self.subTest(backend=backend):
+                config = replace(QWEN35, backends=[backend], context_seqlens=[], context_chunked_shapes=[])
+                cases = list(self.runner.expand_config(config))
+                self.assertEqual(len(cases), count)
+                self.assertEqual({case["page_size"] for case in cases}, pages)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+# then NOTHING: a dense step past 32 rows has no kernel over the pools (the adapter's decline -- an earlier reading, "the prefill kernel
+# serves past the route", was wrong on both counts: the prefill body serves PACKED queries, the EXTEND form).
+_ROUTE_TABLE = {
+    16: {
+        1: (16, 1, True),
+        2: (32, 1, True),
+        3: (32, 2, True),
+        4: (32, 2, True),
+        5: (16, 1, False),
+        16: (16, 1, False),
+        17: (32, 1, False),
+        32: (32, 1, False),
+        33: (0, 0, False),
+    },
+    12: {1: (16, 1, True), 2: (32, 1, True), 3: (32, 2, True), 4: (32, 2, True), 5: (16, 1, False), 33: (0, 0, False)},
+    8: {1: (16, 1, True), 2: (16, 1, True), 3: (32, 1, True), 4: (32, 1, True), 5: (32, 2, True), 8: (32, 2, True), 9: (16, 1, False), 33: (0, 0, False)},
+    6: {1: (16, 1, True), 2: (16, 1, True), 3: (32, 1, True), 5: (32, 1, True), 6: (32, 2, True), 10: (32, 2, True), 11: (16, 1, False), 33: (0, 0, False)},
+    4: {
+        1: (16, 1, True),
+        4: (16, 1, True),
+        5: (32, 1, True),
+        8: (32, 1, True),
+        9: (32, 2, True),
+        16: (32, 2, True),
+        17: (32, 1, False),
+        32: (32, 1, False),
+        33: (0, 0, False),
+    },
+}
+_SENTINEL = 1024.0  # the pools' fill: FINITE (a serving stack's cache is zero-initialized; the tail tile reads and masks the rows past kv_len)
+
+
+def _cc():
+    return tuple(torch.cuda.get_device_capability()) if torch.cuda.is_available() else None
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def _no_host_sync():
+    """Every declaration-time and form check stays on the host without a device sync (Rule 3) -- enforced, not read."""
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        yield
+        return
+    prev = torch.cuda.get_sync_debug_mode()
+    torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode(prev)
+
+
+def _geom(group, heads=None, **over):
+    """The block geometry (and the oracle's mirror) of ``group``: the shrunk matrix's heads, or an explicit ``(h_q, h_kv)`` of that
+    group (the 397B shards at their real ``d_model``, passed through ``over``)."""
+    h_q, h_kv = _GROUPS[group] if heads is None else heads
+    assert h_q % h_kv == 0 and h_q // h_kv == group, (group, heads)
+    kw = dict(d_model=_D_MODEL, h_q=h_q, h_kv=h_kv, d_head=_D, rope_dim=_ROPE, causal_bottom_right=True)
+    kw.update(over)
+    return GatedAttentionBlockGeometry(**kw), RefGeometry(**kw)
+
+
+def _cos(a, b):
+    a, b = a.float().flatten(), b.float().flatten()
+    return (a @ b / (a.norm() * b.norm())).item()
+
+
+def _bits(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """The 16-bit patterns of a bf16 / f16 tensor: a NaN-safe bitwise comparison (the sentinel is NaN)."""
+    return x.contiguous().view(torch.int16)
+
+
+def _pools(n_pages, h, page_size, d, layout, dtype, device=_DEV, fill=None):
+    """Two sentinel-filled pools as ``[P, H, page_size, D]`` views -- ``hnd`` (L1, compact), ``nhd`` (L2, by strides), ``unified``
+    (L3: ONE ``[P, H, page_size, 2D]`` content row per token, K at ``+0``, V at ``+D``).  The fill is a large FINITE value
+    (``_SENTINEL``): the decode tile's tail tile reads the rows past ``kv_len`` (the last page's stale rows, block 0 for the
+    pages a short row does not list) and masks them to ``P = 0`` -- exactly 0 for a finite value, NaN for a NaN one (``0 x
+    NaN``); a serving stack's cache is zero-initialized, so finite is the contract and a big sentinel is the detector of an
+    unmasked read."""
+    fill = _SENTINEL if fill is None else fill
+    if layout == "hnd":
+        return tuple(torch.full((n_pages, h, page_size, d), fill, device=device, dtype=dtype) for _ in range(2))
+    if layout == "nhd":
+        return tuple(torch.full((n_pages, page_size, h, d), fill, device=device, dtype=dtype).permute(0, 2, 1, 3) for _ in range(2))
+    assert layout == "unified"
+    row = torch.full((n_pages, h, page_size, 2 * d), fill, device=device, dtype=dtype)
+    return row[..., :d], row[..., d:]
+
+
+def _make_block(group, batch, s_q, *, page=16, layout="hnd", n_pages=64, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=_DEV, table_row_stride=None, **blk_kw):
+    """A declared (not compiled) DECODE block on EMPTY tensors: the declaration cells."""
+    geom, _ = _geom(group)
+    h_q, h_kv = _GROUPS[group]
+    mk = lambda *shape: torch.empty(*shape, dtype=dtype, device=device)  # noqa: E731
+    kc, vc = _pools(n_pages, h_kv, page, _D, layout, dtype, device)
+    if table_row_stride is None:
+        bt = torch.zeros(batch, n_pages, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    else:
+        bt = torch.zeros(batch, table_row_stride, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)[:, :n_pages]
+    kw = dict(paged_kv_page_size=page, kv_source="paged", sample_k_cache=kc, sample_v_cache=vc, sample_block_table=bt)
+    kw.update(blk_kw)
+    blk = GatedAttentionBlockFwd(
+        mk(batch, s_q, _D_MODEL),
+        mk(geom.n_qkvg, _D_MODEL),
+        torch.ones(_D, dtype=dtype, device=device),
+        torch.ones(_D, dtype=dtype, device=device),
+        mk(batch, s_q, _ROPE),
+        mk(batch, s_q, _ROPE),
+        mk(_D_MODEL, h_q * _D),
+        mk(batch, s_q, _D_MODEL),
+        geom,
+        **kw,
+    )
+    return blk, dict(k_cache=kc, v_cache=vc, block_table=bt, geom=geom)
+

+def test_constants():

+    assert SERVING_PAGE_SIZES == (16, 32, 64, 128) and all(p % 16 == 0 for p in SERVING_PAGE_SIZES)
+    assert SERVING_POOL_LAYOUTS == ("hnd", "nhd", "unified")

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("group", sorted(_GROUPS))
+def test_the_route_table_per_group_and_s_q_is_the_adapters_rule(group):
+    """The decode route at every served group against the adapter's rule: the 16-column tile for <= 16 packed rows, the
+    32-column tile in ``ceil(S_q / (32 // G))`` token units up to two, then the UNPACKED arm (one head per CTA) up to 32
+    rows, NOT SERVED past that (the reason names the EXTEND form); the CLAIMED envelope is ``S_q <= 4`` everywhere, the
+    wider cells routed but not claimed.  MHA stays unpacked."""
+    geom, _ = _geom(group)
+    for s_q, (n_q, units, packed) in _ROUTE_TABLE[group].items():
+        r = decode_route(geom, s_q)
+        assert isinstance(r, DecodeRoute) and r.s_q == s_q and r.group == group
+        assert (r.n_q, r.token_units, r.pack_gqa) == (n_q, units, packed), (group, s_q, r)
+        assert r.tile == (DECODE_TILE if n_q else None) and r.decode_tile is bool(n_q) and r.served is bool(n_q)
+        assert (r.reason == "") is bool(n_q) and ("EXTEND form" in r.reason or n_q)
+        assert r.claimed is (packed and s_q <= DECODE_MAX_S_Q)
+        if packed:
+            assert units == -(-s_q // (n_q // group))
+        elif n_q:
+            assert units == 1 and s_q <= n_q
+    mha = GatedAttentionBlockGeometry(d_model=_D_MODEL, h_q=4, h_kv=4, d_head=_D, rope_dim=_ROPE, causal_bottom_right=True)
+    r = decode_route(mha, 2)
+    assert (r.group, r.n_q, r.token_units, r.pack_gqa) == (1, 16, 1, False)
+    d128 = GatedAttentionBlockGeometry(d_model=_D_MODEL, h_q=8, h_kv=2, d_head=128, rope_dim=_ROPE, causal_bottom_right=True)
+    assert not decode_route(d128, 1).served and "d_head=128" in decode_route(d128, 1).reason  # no decode tile outside the d256 flavor

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Rubin: the cells
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+_SPLIT = 128  # the SDPA's KV tile
+
+
+def _rope_tables(n_pos, dtype, geom_ref):
+    cos, sin = build_rope_tables(n_pos, _ROPE, base=geom_ref.rope_base, batch=1, device=_DEV, dtype=dtype)
+    return cos, sin  # [1, n_pos, ROPE]
+
+
+class _Case:
+    """One DECODE step over a batch of sequences with lengths ``kv_lens`` (0 = a padded entry): the inputs of the whole
+    sequence per entry, the step's inputs (the last ``s_q`` rows), the sentinel-filled pools pre-filled with the ORACLE's
+    prefix K / V, the block table (block 0 = the NULL block, never allocated), the slot mapping of the step's tokens (-1 on a
+    padded entry), and the per-sequence fp32 oracle of the step's ``out`` rows."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        group,
+        s_q,
+        kv_lens,
+        *,
+        page=16,
+        layout="hnd",
+        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        seed=0,
+        n_pages=None,
+        table_row_stride=None,
+        blk_kw=None,
+        heads=None,
+        d_model=None,
+    ):
+        self.group, self.s_q, self.kv_lens, self.page, self.layout, self.dtype = group, int(s_q), [int(x) for x in kv_lens], page, layout, dtype
+        self.d_model = _D_MODEL if d_model is None else int(d_model)  # the shrunk matrix width, or a shard's real one
+        self.geom, self.ref_geom = _geom(group, heads=heads, d_model=self.d_model)
+        h_q, h_kv = _GROUPS[group] if heads is None else heads
+        g = torch.Generator(device=_DEV).manual_seed(seed)
+        B = len(self.kv_lens)
+        assert all(L == 0 or L >= s_q for L in self.kv_lens), "a live entry holds at least the step's tokens"
+        L_max = max(max(self.kv_lens), s_q)
+
+        def randn(*shape, std=0.02):
+            return (torch.randn(*shape, generator=g, device=_DEV, dtype=torch.float32) * std).to(dtype)
+
+        self.w = dict(
+            w_qkvg=randn(self.geom.n_qkvg, self.d_model),
+            w_q_norm=torch.ones(_D, dtype=dtype, device=_DEV),
+            w_k_norm=torch.ones(_D, dtype=dtype, device=_DEV),
+            w_o=randn(self.d_model, h_q * _D),
+        )
+        cos_t, sin_t = _rope_tables(L_max, dtype, self.ref_geom)
+        self.h_full = [randn(1, max(L, s_q), self.d_model, std=1.0) for L in self.kv_lens]
+        # the step's inputs: the LAST s_q rows (and their positions' RoPE rows); a padded entry takes its row 0 .. s_q-1 (never read)
+        self.h = torch.stack([hf[0, -s_q:] for hf in self.h_full])  # [B, s_q, d_model]
+        pos = [list(range(L - s_q, L)) if L else list(range(s_q)) for L in self.kv_lens]
+        self.cos = torch.stack([cos_t[0, p] for p in pos])
+        self.sin = torch.stack([sin_t[0, p] for p in pos])
+        # the oracle per live entry over the FULL sequence: its K / V rows (bf16 -- the oracle's single rounding) fill the pools
+        self.ref_out = torch.zeros(B, s_q, self.d_model, dtype=dtype, device=_DEV)
+        self.ref_rows = {}
+        for b, L in enumerate(self.kv_lens):
+            if L == 0:
+                continue
+            ref = gated_attention_block_reference(
+                self.h_full[b], self.w["w_qkvg"], self.w["w_q_norm"], self.w["w_k_norm"], cos_t[:, :L], sin_t[:, :L], self.w["w_o"], self.ref_geom
+            )
+            self.ref_out[b] = ref.out[0, -s_q:]
+            self.ref_rows[b] = (ref.k[0], ref.v[0])  # [L, h_kv, D]
+        # pages: block 0 reserved (NULL); each live entry gets ceil(L / P) pages from a permutation of 1 .. n_pages-1
+        need = sum(-(-L // page) for L in self.kv_lens)
+        self.n_pages = n_pages if n_pages is not None else need + 1 + 2
+        assert self.n_pages >= need + 1, (self.n_pages, need)
+        perm = (torch.randperm(self.n_pages - 1, generator=g, device=_DEV) + 1).tolist()
+        max_pages = max(-(-L_max // page), 1)
+        table_cols = max_pages if table_row_stride is None else table_row_stride
+        assert table_cols >= max_pages
+        big = torch.zeros(B, table_cols, dtype=torch.int32, device=_DEV)
+        self.block_table = big[:, :max_pages]
+        self.max_kv_len = max_pages * page
+        it = iter(perm)
+        slots = torch.full((B * s_q,), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=_DEV)
+        self.k_cache, self.v_cache = _pools(self.n_pages, h_kv, page, _D, layout, dtype)
+        for b, L in enumerate(self.kv_lens):
+            if L == 0:
+                continue  # the padded entry: row 0 (the NULL block), slots -1
+            pages = [next(it) for _ in range(-(-L // page))]
+            self.block_table[b, : len(pages)] = torch.tensor(pages, dtype=torch.int32, device=_DEV)
+            k_rows, v_rows = self.ref_rows[b]
+            for p in range(L - s_q):  # the PREFIX: the oracle's rows into the pools
+                pg, off = pages[p // page], p % page
+                self.k_cache[pg, :, off] = k_rows[p]
+                self.v_cache[pg, :, off] = v_rows[p]
+            for i in range(s_q):  # the step's tokens: written through by the block
+                p = L - s_q + i
+                slots[b * s_q + i] = pages[p // page] * page + p % page
+        self.slot_mapping = slots
+        self.kv_lens_t = torch.tensor(self.kv_lens, dtype=torch.int32, device=_DEV)
+        self.block0_bits = _bits(self.k_cache[0]).clone(), _bits(self.v_cache[0]).clone()
+        self.live = torch.tensor([L > 0 for L in self.kv_lens], device=_DEV)
+        # the fused norm + RoPE fork is rendered for bf16 only: f16 cells run the unfused (1) then (2)+(3)
+        kw = dict(
+            paged_kv_page_size=page,
+            kv_source="paged",
+            sample_k_cache=self.k_cache,
+            sample_v_cache=self.v_cache,
+            sample_block_table=self.block_table,
+            fuse_gate=True,
+            fuse_norm_rope=dtype == torch.bfloat16,
+        )
+        kw.update(blk_kw or {})
+        self.blk_kw = kw
+        self.out = torch.empty(B, s_q, self.d_model, dtype=dtype, device=_DEV)
+        self.blk = GatedAttentionBlockFwd(
+            self.h, self.w["w_qkvg"], self.w["w_q_norm"], self.w["w_k_norm"], self.cos, self.sin, self.w["w_o"], self.out, self.geom, **kw
+        )
+        self.ws = None
+
+    def compile(self):
+        self.blk.check_support()
+        self.blk.compile()
+        self.ws = torch.empty(self.blk.get_workspace_size(), dtype=torch.uint8, device=_DEV)
+        return self
+
+    def execute(self, *, out=None, ws=None, h=None, cos=None, sin=None, kv_lens=None, block_table=None, slot_mapping=None, stream=None):
+        out = self.out if out is None else out
+        self.blk.execute(
+            self.h if h is None else h,
+            self.w["w_qkvg"],
+            self.w["w_q_norm"],
+            self.w["w_k_norm"],
+            self.cos if cos is None else cos,
+            self.sin if sin is None else sin,
+            self.w["w_o"],
+            out,
+            self.ws if ws is None else ws,
+            k_cache=self.k_cache,
+            v_cache=self.v_cache,
+            block_table=self.block_table if block_table is None else block_table,
+            kv_lens=self.kv_lens_t if kv_lens is None else kv_lens,
+            slot_mapping=self.slot_mapping if slot_mapping is None else slot_mapping,
+            current_stream=stream,
+        )
+        return out
+
+    def run(self):
+        if self.ws is None:
+            self.compile()
+        self.execute()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        return self.out
+
+    # -- views of the block's intermediates after an execute --------------------------------------------------------------
+    def slab_views(self, ws=None):
+        """The post-norm-RoPE Q band and the GATE band of the slab the last execute left in the workspace, as the SDPA's
+        ``[B, S_q, H_q, D]`` views (the slab's token stride), and the O slot."""
+        ws = self.ws if ws is None else ws
+        g, lay = self.geom, self.blk._ws
+        t = self.blk.batch * self.blk.seq_len
+        proj = _view(ws, lay.proj, (t, g.n_qkvg), self.dtype)
+        o_q, o_g = g.qkvg_offsets[:2]
+        q = _cols(proj, o_q, g.h_q, g.d_head).view(self.blk.batch, self.blk.seq_len, g.h_q, g.d_head)
+        gate = _cols(proj, o_g, g.h_q, g.d_head).view(self.blk.batch, self.blk.seq_len, g.h_q, g.d_head)
+        o = _view(ws, lay.o, (t, g.h_q, g.d_head), self.dtype).view(self.blk.batch, self.blk.seq_len, g.h_q, g.d_head)
+        return q, gate, o, ws[lay.engine_scratch :]
+
+    def check_against_oracle(self, out=None, *, what="out"):
+        out = self.out if out is None else out
+        assert torch.isfinite(out.float()).all(), f"{what}: non-finite"
+        dead = ~self.live
+        if dead.any():
+            assert (out[dead] == 0).all(), f"{what}: a padded entry (kv_lens = 0) must yield out rows EXACTLY 0"
+        c = _cos(out[self.live], self.ref_out[self.live])
+        md = (out[self.live].float() - self.ref_out[self.live].float()).abs().max().item()
+        print(f"[{self.group}/{self.s_q} p{self.page} {self.layout} {self.dtype} lens={self.kv_lens}] {what} vs oracle cos {c:.6f} max|diff| {md:.3e}")
+        assert c > 0.999, f"{what}: cos {c}"
+        return c, md
+
+    def route_readback(self):
+        """What the adapter COMPILED, read back: the kernel template, the module's packing / split / gate facts."""
+        impl = self.blk._sdpa._impl
+        mod = impl._k_mod
+        return dict(
+            template=impl.kernel_template,
+            file=mod.__file__,
+            heads_per_tile=getattr(mod, "HEADS_PER_TILE", None),
+            split=getattr(getattr(mod, "CFG", None), "SPLIT_KV", None),
+            epilogue_gate=getattr(getattr(mod, "PARAMS", None), "epilogue_gate", None),
+            n_q=getattr(getattr(mod, "CFG", None), "N_Q", None),
+            adapter_split=impl.split_kv,
+            adapter_pack=impl.pack_gqa,
+        )
+
+
+_CASES = {}
+
+
+def _case(key, *args, **kw):
+    if key not in _CASES:
+        _CASES[key] = _Case(*args, **kw).compile()
+    return _CASES[key]
+
+
+# kv_lens of the standard cell: one KV tile (100: a tail tile too), ring depth 3 (384 = 3 tiles exactly), ring depth 4 with a
+# tail (500), a PADDED entry (0: block 0 + slot -1) -- kv_lens > S_q on every live row at S_q <= 5.
+_LENS = (100, 384, 500, 0)
+
+
+def _std_case(group, s_q, **kw):
+    return _case(("std", group, s_q) + tuple(sorted(kw.items())), group, s_q, _LENS, **kw)
+

+@requires_rubin
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("group", sorted(_GROUPS))
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("s_q", [1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
+def test_decode_matches_the_oracle_at_every_group_and_s_q(group, s_q):
+    """The DECODE cells of the served-group matrix: every served group x S_q 1 .. 4 (the claimed envelope) and S_q = 5 (past the packed route at 16 /
+    12: the adapter's UNPACKED tile, one head per CTA; the packed tile's second token unit at 8 / 6 -- correct and DECLARED),
+    against the per-sequence fp32 oracle under the dense
+    suite's budget (cos > 0.999 on ``out``), the padded entry EXACTLY 0 with block 0 untouched, the route pinned against the
+    compiled kernel (its template, packing, split and the gate OUT of the kernel: in the combine)."""
+    case = _std_case(group, s_q)
+    case.run()
+    case.check_against_oracle()

+        sample_q=q.transpose(1, 2),

+        sample_v=sample_v,

+def _ulp(mag, mbits):
+    """The output dtype's ulp at each element's binade, floored at the subnormal step (the decode suite's helper)."""
+    _, exp = torch.frexp(mag.cpu())
+    emin = {7: -126, 10: -14}[mbits]
+    ulp = torch.ldexp(torch.ones_like(mag.cpu()), exp - 1 - mbits)
+    return torch.clamp(ulp, min=2.0 ** (emin - mbits)).to(mag.device)
+

+def _pre_gate_o(case, split):
+    """The pre-gate O of the block's own stage (4) at ``split`` on the block's post-execute slab views: a fresh ungated stage
+    declared like the block's (the gate OFF: the combine applies none), executed into its own buffer."""
+    api, o_buf, q, _ = _adapter_like(case, sample_k=case.k_cache, sample_v=case.v_cache, paged=True, gate=False, split=split, lse=True)
+    lse = torch.empty(case.blk.batch, case.geom.h_q, case.blk.seq_len, dtype=torch.float32, device=_DEV)
+    ws = torch.empty(max(api.scratch_workspace_bytes(), 1), dtype=torch.uint8, device=_DEV)
+    api.execute(
+        q.transpose(1, 2),
+        case.k_cache,
+        case.v_cache,
+        o_buf.transpose(1, 2),
+        lse_tensor=lse,
+        seq_kv_lens=case.kv_lens_t,
+        block_table=case.block_table,
+        workspace=ws,
+    )
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    return o_buf, lse, api

+def _split_budget(case, a, b, q_rows):
+    """The decode suite's two-term budget between a split and an unsplit plan, per O element, generalized to S_q >= 1 with
+    the bottom-right band: ``|a - b| <= ulp(max(|a|, |b|)) + 2 eps_P sum_j p_j |v_j| / l`` -- one output rounding of two
+    differently associated fp32 sums, plus twice the half-precision P quantization each path does at its own running max,
+    weighted by the row's softmax-mean |V| (computed from the same pools in fp32)."""
+    mbits = {torch.bfloat16: 7, torch.float16: 10}[case.dtype]
+    eps_p = 2.0 ** -(mbits + 1)
+    B, s_q, H, d = q_rows.shape
+    KH, P = _GROUPS[case.group][1], case.page
+    G = H // KH
+    budget = torch.zeros(B, s_q, H, d, dtype=torch.float64, device=_DEV)
+    live = torch.zeros(B, s_q, H, dtype=torch.bool, device=_DEV)
+    for bi, L in enumerate(case.kv_lens):
+        if L == 0:
+            continue
+        pages = case.block_table[bi, : -(-L // P)].tolist()
+        k = torch.cat([case.k_cache[pg] for pg in pages], dim=1)[:, :L].float()  # [KH, L, d]
+        v = torch.cat([case.v_cache[pg] for pg in pages], dim=1)[:, :L].float().abs()
+        kv_h = torch.arange(H, device=_DEV) // G
+        qf = q_rows[bi].float()  # [s_q, H, d]
+        scores = torch.einsum("shd,hLd->shL", qf, k[kv_h]) * case.geom.scale  # [s_q, H, L]
+        keys = torch.arange(L, device=_DEV)
+        allowed = keys[None, :] <= (torch.arange(s_q, device=_DEV) + (L - s_q))[:, None]  # bottom-right
+        scores = scores.masked_fill(~allowed[:, None, :], float("-inf"))
+        prob = torch.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
+        pv_abs = torch.einsum("shL,hLd->shd", prob.nan_to_num(0.0), v[kv_h])
+        budget[bi] = (2.0 * eps_p) * pv_abs.double()
+        live[bi] = torch.isfinite(prob).all(dim=-1)
+    a64, b64 = a.double(), b.double()
+    mag = torch.maximum(a64.abs(), b64.abs())
+    budget = budget + _ulp(mag, mbits)
+    diff = (a64 - b64).abs()
+    m = live.unsqueeze(-1).expand_as(diff)
+    return diff[m], budget[m]

+def test_the_gate_in_the_combine_vs_the_separate_gate_launch_within_one_rounding(dtype):
+    """``fuse_gate=True`` (the gate applied to the merged fp32 value in the split COMBINE, one rounding) vs ``fuse_gate=False``
+    at the SAME split (the tile's bf16 / f16 O, then stage (5): ``round(O * sigmoid(G))`` -- two roundings and its own approx
+    sigmoid), per element of O: ``|a - r| <= ulp(max(|a|, |r|)) + sigmoid(g) ulp(|b|) / 2 + |b| 2^-11`` with ``b`` the pre-gate
+    O (the decode suite's stated budget: the two final roundings, the intermediate rounding the unfused path carries, and the
+    approximate tanh behind both sigmoids).  The exact max |diff| is the record; ``out`` of both within the suite's budget."""
+    lens = (1000, 0, 384, 77)
+    fused = _case(("gate", dtype, "combine"), 16, 2, lens, dtype=dtype, seed=19)
+    split = fused.blk.decode_split_kv
+    unfused = _case(("gate", dtype, "launch"), 16, 2, lens, dtype=dtype, seed=19, blk_kw=dict(fuse_gate=False, decode_split_kv=split))
+    assert fused.blk.gate_fused and not unfused.blk.gate_fused and unfused.blk.decode_split_kv == split >= 2
+    out_f, out_u = fused.run().clone(), unfused.run().clone()
+    fused.check_against_oracle(what="gate-in-combine")
+    unfused.check_against_oracle(what="gate launch")
+    q_f, gate_f, o_f, _ = fused.slab_views()
+    q_u, gate_u, o_u, _ = unfused.slab_views()
+    assert torch.equal(q_f, q_u) and torch.equal(gate_f, gate_u)
+    b, _, _ = _pre_gate_o(unfused, split)  # the ungated merged O the separate launch gated
+    mbits = {torch.bfloat16: 7, torch.float16: 10}[dtype]
+    a, r, b64 = o_f.double(), o_u.double(), b.double()
+    s = torch.sigmoid(gate_f.double())
+    live = fused.live.view(-1, 1, 1, 1).expand_as(a)
+    budget = _ulp(torch.maximum(a.abs(), r.abs()), mbits) + s * _ulp(b64.abs(), mbits) * 0.5 + b64.abs() * 2.0**-11
+    diff = (a - r).abs()
+    ratio = (diff[live] / budget[live]).max().item()
+    print(
+        f"[{dtype}] gate-in-combine vs the separate gate launch (split {split}): max |diff| {diff[live].max().item():.3e} on |O| up to "
+        f"{r[live].abs().max().item():.3f}, {(diff[live] > 0).double().mean().item():.4%} of the live elements differ, max |diff| / budget {ratio:.3f}; "
+        f"out: cos {_cos(out_f[fused.live], out_u[fused.live]):.6f} max |diff| {(out_f.float() - out_u.float()).abs().max().item():.3e}"
+    )
+    assert ratio <= 1.0, ratio

+def test_capture_of_the_first_execute_replays_bitwise_and_takes_new_lengths_tables_slots_and_inputs():
+    """The serving stack's defaults: the FIRST execute of a fresh declaration captured on a NEW stream with no eager warm-up
+    under ``set_sync_debug_mode("error")`` (no host sync in the DECODE path: lengths, tables and slots are device data); the
+    capture launches nothing, the replay is BITWISE a fresh eager run; a padded batch replays correctly; new ``kv_lens`` /
+    ``block_table`` / ``slot_mapping`` / ``h`` through the captured tensors replay bitwise the eager run over them."""
+    lens = (300, 0, 1000, 77)
+    case = _Case(16, 2, lens, seed=23)  # fresh: never executed
+    case.blk.check_support()
+    case.blk.compile()
+    case.ws = torch.empty(case.blk.get_workspace_size(), dtype=torch.uint8, device=_DEV)
+    case.out.fill_(float("nan"))
+    k_before = _written(case.k_cache)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    try:
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=stream):
+            prev = torch.cuda.get_sync_debug_mode()
+            torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")
+            try:
+                case.execute()  # the FIRST execute of this declaration, captured
+            finally:
+                torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode(prev)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        assert torch.isnan(case.out).all() and _written(case.k_cache) == k_before, "the capture launched work"
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        replayed = case.out.clone()
+        case.check_against_oracle(replayed, what="replay")
+        # eager over the same inputs: the pools already hold the step's tokens (idempotent rows), out bitwise
+        case.out.fill_(float("nan"))
+        case.execute()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        assert torch.equal(case.out, replayed), "the replay of the captured first execute differs from the eager run"
+        # a NEW step through the captured tensors: new lengths (one entry longer by a token: its slot moves), a re-laid-out
+        # table (pages swapped between two entries), new slots and new h -- the oracle of the new step through a sibling case
+        sib = _Case(16, 2, (301, 0, 1000, 77), seed=29, table_row_stride=case.block_table.shape[1])
+        # the sibling's pools hold its oracle prefix; make the CAPTURED pools hold them (the captured pointers are the block's)

+        case.v_cache.copy_(sib.v_cache)
+        case.block_table.copy_(sib.block_table)
+        case.kv_lens_t.copy_(sib.kv_lens_t)
+        case.slot_mapping.copy_(sib.slot_mapping)
+        case.h.copy_(sib.h)
+        case.cos.copy_(sib.cos)
+        case.sin.copy_(sib.sin)
+        case.w["w_qkvg"].copy_(sib.w["w_qkvg"])
+        case.w["w_o"].copy_(sib.w["w_o"])
+        case.out.fill_(float("nan"))
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        replayed2 = case.out.clone()
+        assert torch.isfinite(replayed2.float()).all() and (replayed2[1] == 0).all()
+        c = _cos(replayed2[sib.live], sib.ref_out[sib.live])
+        print(f"replay over new lengths / table / slots / inputs vs the new step's oracle: cos {c:.6f}")
+        assert c > 0.999
+        case.out.fill_(float("nan"))
+        case.execute()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        assert torch.equal(case.out, replayed2), "the replay over new lengths / tables / slots differs from the eager run over them"
+    finally:
+        graph.reset()
